conversation.content:
Hi there—I’m so glad we’re connecting. I’m Sarah, a perinatal mental-health clinician, and my job is to listen without judgment and to make sure you’re getting the support you deserve in these early weeks of motherhood. Today we’re going to use a brief, well-trusted tool called the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale, or EPDS. It’s simply ten questions about how you’ve been feeling over the past seven days. There are no right or wrong answers; whatever you share stays strictly between us (unless you tell me something that makes me worry about your immediate safety, in which case we’ll talk through next steps together). We’ll take it one question at a time, and you can answer in your own words. Ready to begin?

First question: Over the last seven days, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things, or has that felt difficult?

[soft half-smile]  
I can still laugh—like when my husband made that silly face trying to get the baby to smile—but it’s not the same easy, big laugh I used to have. It feels… muffled, I guess. Most of the time I’m just too tired or distracted to find things funny, even when I know they’re supposed to be.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things
Yeah... I can still laugh sometimes, but it's not the same. It's like I have to remind myself to find things funny, and even when I do laugh, it feels kind of forced or doesn't last long.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

[slow shrug]  
I *want* to look forward to stuff—like our Sunday coffee run or the new show everyone’s talking about—but it feels flat. I’ll think, “Okay, that could be nice,” yet when the moment comes, I’m kind of going through the motions. The excitement isn’t really there like it used to be.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

[eyes drop to hands]  
Yeah… a couple of times this week. Yesterday the baby wouldn’t settle for his nap and I kept thinking, “I must be doing something wrong—maybe I’m not reading his cues right.” I know rationally babies just fuss, but the thought still jumps in that I’m falling short somehow.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Sometimes my mind just races out of nowhere—like I’ll be folding laundry and suddenly worry that the baby’s breathing sounds different, even though he’s right next to me and fine. I can usually talk myself down pretty quickly, but those “what-if” moments pop up a few times a day.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason
Not really panicky… more like a quick flutter of “something bad could happen.” It passes fast, and I haven’t had any full-blown scares, just that little jolt of worry that catches me off guard.
Things have been getting on top of me

[lets out a shaky breath]  
Some days, yeah. When the baby’s extra fussy and the dishes pile up, I feel this tightness in my chest like everything’s stacking higher than I can reach. I usually manage to push through, but it’s like I’m wading through thick mud just to finish one task.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

I’ve been sleeping okay once I get to bed, but I do lie there for a while with my mind circling—worrying about whether I’m doing enough or if something might be wrong with the baby. It takes maybe half an hour to settle, so I end up getting less rest, but I’m not wide-awake all night or anything.
I have felt sad or miserable

I do feel a bit down some days—like there’s this dull heaviness that just sits there. It’s not all the time, and I still have okay moments, but the sadness sneaks in, especially when I’m alone with the baby and everything feels quiet and overwhelming.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

[eyes water a little]  
Yes… twice this week. Once when the baby wouldn’t latch and I felt completely useless, and again yesterday when my mom left after dropping off groceries—just this wave of “I can’t do this” hit me and the tears came before I could stop them.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

[shakes head quickly]  
No—never. I’ve felt overwhelmed and cried, but I haven’t had any thoughts like that.

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 16: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Note  

Patient-reported symptoms (≥2 wks):  
- Persistent low mood, “dull heaviness,” frequent tearfulness (2 crying spells this week)  
- Marked anhedonia: laughter feels forced, anticipatory enjoyment “flat”  
- Excessive self-blame/guilt re infant care (“I must be doing something wrong”)  
- Recurrent intrusive “what-if” worries (baby’s breathing, adequacy as mother) 3–4× daily  
- Episodic chest tightness and feeling “overwhelmed” by routine tasks  
- Initial insomnia (≈30 min sleep-onset delay) driven by ruminative worry  

Pattern: Symptoms cluster in evening/night when alone with infant; no functional impairment in basic self-care or infant care; no self-harm ideation.  

Screening significance: Positive indicators for mild–moderate postpartum depression with comorbid anxiety; rule-out formal major depressive episode and generalized anxiety disorder. Safety risk: Denies self-harm; no protective concerns noted today.
